paragraphs: SetTimer takes packed BCD minutes and seconds ($MMSS), not binary seconds.
Clear the old countdown before loading the duration and startup state.
SetTimer takes packed BCD minutes and seconds ($MMSS), not binary seconds.
Startup begins with an initial delay before the timer display moves into place.
The reset vector enters in emulation mode. Switch to native mode and the
bank-$80 FastROM mirror, establish the stack and direct page, then initialise
low RAM and the display. Upload the SPC engine before joining CommonBootSection.
The polling delay below is retained as written; its original purpose is unknown.
Cold boot and SoftReset converge here. Force blank, clear bank $7E and initialise
CPU/PPU shadows, sound queues and sprite-transfer state before enabling NMI.
Finish the SRAM/demo checks, then jump to MainGameLoop without a return address.
NMI may run before the first frame request; its no-request path skips uploads.
Set NMI_Request only after the caller's frame buffers and transfer queues are
ready. NMI clears it after uploads and controller sampling, releasing this
busy-wait. An NMI with no request takes the lag path instead of consuming
partially prepared data. NMI must be enabled or this routine cannot finish.
Processor flags and the data bank are restored; A is used by the polling loop
and byte-index mode truncates the high bytes of X and Y.
Set bit 7 in both $4200 and its shared DP_IRQAutoJoy shadow. Preserve the
h/v-counter interrupt and auto-joypad bits. This is separate from CLI/SEI:
the CPU's IRQ-disable flag does not enable or disable NMI.
Clear bit 7 in both $4200 and DP_IRQAutoJoy, preserving the other control bits.
Keeping the shadow in sync matters because Update_IO_Registers uploads it again.
A subsequent WaitForNMI requires NMI to be re-enabled.
The native NMI vector enters through bank $00; jump to the bank-$80 mirror,
save full-width registers and establish direct page $0000 before doing work.
A nonzero NMI_Request gates the prepared-frame transfers and input sampling.
Servicing it clears the request and lag count and advances NMI_8bitFrameCounter
and NMI_FrameCounter. NMI_Counter advances on both serviced and lag paths.
RTI restores the interrupted processor status as well as its program address.
Refresh the table-address registers for six HDMA-object slots. The object index
steps by two; each active slot supplies a DMA-channel offset and a word pointer.
Later, DP_HDMAEnable is written to $420C after the queued VRAM transfers.
No frame is ready. Leave transfer queues and sampled controller state untouched;
increment the byte-sized consecutive lag count and its unsigned high-water mark.
The count wraps at $100; the high-water mark is retained across that wrap.
Rejoin the common exit to count this NMI and restore the interrupted context
without advancing the serviced-frame counters.
Dispatch h/v-counter IRQ commands for scanline effects such as the HUD split
and door-transition drawing. DP_IRQCmd is already a word-table byte offset.
The command returns its successor in A, the next horizontal target in X and
vertical target in Y. Store all three before restoring the interrupted registers.
Unlike NMI, this entry does not change the direct-page base; direct-page command
state uses the engine's existing direct page.
Called near the end of a serviced NMI, after the graphics work. Wait until the
auto-joypad busy bit clears before reading the controller result. Derive newly
pressed buttons from current AND (current XOR previous), then maintain held
button repeat state. The no-request NMI path does not call this routine.
Reload gameplay graphics while interrupts are controlled for direct VRAM work.
Mask IRQs, stop DMA, disable NMI and h/v-counter interrupts, then rebuild CRE,
tileset, background, visible-room and PLM graphics. Re-enable the interrupt
sources and restore the caller's saved bank and processor status before RTL.
Consume the seven-byte VRAMWrite records prepared by main-thread systems.
VRAMWriteStack is the byte offset after the last record; write a zero-size
terminator there, then walk records from offset zero. Each record supplies a
word size, 24-bit source and VRAM destination to DMA channel 1 in mode 1.
The destination word's sign bit selects the VRAM increment mode. A clear bit
uses $80, advancing one word after the high-byte write; a set bit uses $81,
advancing 32 words for column uploads. Write the same destination to VMADD,
trigger channel 1, then advance seven bytes to the next software record.
Reset the ordinary write-table stack after consuming it. Horizontal and
vertical scrolling buffers are independent flag-driven queues, so process
both even when VRAMWriteStack was already zero. The caller's processor
status is restored after all three upload paths finish.
Upload newly exposed BG1 columns with VMAIN $81: DMA writes each word's low
and high bytes, then advances 32 VRAM words to the next tilemap row. Separate
left/right staging buffers target adjacent columns. Upload the unwrapped
segment first, followed by the optional segment that wrapped in tilemap VRAM.
BG2 repeats the BG1 column geometry with its own flag, sizes, destinations and
bank-$7E staging buffers. Clear the flag before DMA so this prepared update is
consumed once. A zero wrapped size skips only the wrapped pair; the unwrapped
left/right transfers have already completed.
Upload newly exposed BG1 rows with VMAIN $80, advancing one VRAM word after
each tilemap word. The top-half buffer uses the prepared destination; OR $20
selects the next 32-word tile row for the bottom-half buffer. Repeat that pair
from adjusted sources and a second destination when the row wraps in VRAM.
BG2 has the same top/bottom and unwrapped/wrapped row layout as BG1, using its
own prepared buffers. Every transfer uses WRAM bank $7E and DMA channel 1.
Clear the update flag once, then a zero wrapped size bypasses the wrapped pair
without affecting the unwrapped upload already sent.
The preceding SEP #$02 sets the processor's zero flag, so BEQ always skips
this self-loop on a conforming 65816. Preserve the loop as an unreachable
status-flag sentinel from the original program; it is not a data-dependent
failure check in the normal BG2 wrapped-row transfer.
Consume nine-byte VRAMRead records during the serviced NMI path. A record
provides the VRAM word address, DMA mode and B-bus target, 24-bit WRAM
destination and byte count. Channel 1 performs the VRAM-to-WRAM transfer,
then the reader advances by the exact nine-byte software-record stride.
VRAMReadStack is the byte offset after the final record. With the accumulator
still eight-bit, STZ writes only one zero byte at that offset, but the loop
later tests a word source after REP #$20. This retained mismatch is safe only
when the following byte is already zero; normal producers queue one read.
Scan all eight word-sized timer slots from offset $0E down to zero. Carry is
set when any slot has a nonzero timer and clear only when every timer is zero.
This reports queued countdowns; it does not inspect the active music timer,
the ring indices or whether the SPC is currently playing a track.
Advance the active music countdown and the eight-slot word-indexed ring.
A positive timer keeps waiting, zero dispatches the active entry, and a
negative timer loads the next queued entry. When the ring is empty, store
zero so the next call underflows and checks the queue again.
A nonnegative entry is an SPC track request. Send its low seven bits through
$2140, mirror the track number and suppress sound-effect handshakes for eight
calls. Clear the consumed ring slot, advance its byte offset by two modulo
$10, then immediately load the next queued entry if one exists.
A negative entry selects a music-data upload by its low byte. Build the
24-bit source from overlapping words in Music_Pointers and synchronously
upload it to the SPC. Mark $FF while uploading, then clear the marker, consume
the ring slot and impose eight calls of sound-effect downtime before returning.
Queue a word-sized track or music-data request with an eight-call delay.
Reject demo game states ($28 and above), and reserve one of the eight ring
slots so the wrapped next index can never equal the consumer index. A full
ring drops this request without changing entries or either cursor.
Queue the request at the current producer offset with max(Y, 8) calls of
delay. Demo states are still rejected, but this variant does not compare the
next and start indices before writing. It can overwrite an unread slot and
always advances the producer by one word modulo the eight-slot ring.
Store either Y or the clamped minimum of eight in the timer slot paired with
the request. Advance the word offset by two and mask with $000E, producing
the ring sequence $00, $02, ... $0E, $00 without a capacity check.
The library-1 wrappers preserve X, Y and status, switch to byte registers and
move the caller's sound ID into A high. Loading 15, 9, 6, 3 or 1 into A low
selects the maximum outstanding count before branching into the common body.
The common return restores the stack frame created by whichever wrapper ran.
Queue one library-1 sound when its modulo-16 outstanding count is below the
wrapper's threshold. XBA recovers the sound ID after the count check. Global
sound disable, demo states and an active power-bomb explosion each reject the
request before any ring byte or producer index changes.
Y is the current producer slot and X is its wrapped successor. When advancing
would not collide with the consumer, store the sound at Y, publish X as the
new producer and clear that next slot as the queue sentinel.
The retained physical-full path calls an empty hook, then compares the new
sound ID with the byte at the current producer slot. Only a numerically lower
ID replaces that byte, and the producer index remains unchanged. Official
threshold wrappers normally reject a consistent full ring before this path.
Library-2 wrappers use the same packed A convention and thresholds as library
1: the sound ID moves into A high and the maximum outstanding count occupies
A low. The common library-2 body restores X, Y and status on every exit.
Apply the threshold and global sound gates to library 2's independent start,
next and 16-byte ring. The arithmetic and control flow mirror library 1, but
all capacity state and payload bytes belong exclusively to library 2.
Commit a library-2 request only when the wrapped successor does not equal its
consumer index. The published next slot is cleared after insertion, retaining
the zero sentinel expected by subsequent producers.
The library-2 full-ring branch shares the empty hook and numeric comparison.
A lower ID may replace the current producer byte without advancing the ring;
an equal or higher ID is discarded through the common restoring return.
Library-3 wrappers repeat the packed sound/threshold ABI and shared restore
frame. Their only data difference is the independent library-3 metadata and
payload ring selected by the common body below.
Apply the same modulo-16 threshold, global-disable, demo and power-bomb gates
to library 3. Successful requests modify only its producer index and 16-byte
queue; the consumer later sends them through SPC port $2143.
Store the library-3 sound at its current producer slot, advance modulo 16 and
clear the new producer slot when that advance does not collide with the start.
On the retained library-3 collision path, keep the producer fixed and replace
its current byte only when the new sound ID is numerically lower. All exits
restore the wrapper's processor status, Y and X in that order.
Decode the eight data bytes placed immediately after the caller's JSL:
channel, DMA mode, B-bus target, 24-bit source and 16-bit byte count.
The helper selects that channel's $43x0 register block, writes the descriptor
without starting DMA, then advances the stacked return address past the data.
Map channel numbers 0..7 to the corresponding $4300..$4370 register-block
offset. Callers still start the configured transfer through $420B or $420C.
Publish the prepared CPU/PPU shadow bytes during the serviced NMI. Ordinary
registers are copied once; scroll and Mode 7 words are sent low byte then high
byte through the hardware write latches. Gameplay screen and colour-math copies
retain the values actually presented by this frame.
Upload the four Mode 7 matrix coefficients and two origins only when either the
real or fake BG-mode shadow selects mode 7. Each word uses the PPU register's
two-write latch, preserving the matrix/origin state prepared outside NMI.
Configure channel 0 to copy all $220 bytes of the software OAM image to $2104
and channel 1 to copy the full $200-byte palette image to $2122. Reset both
hardware destinations to zero, then start the two independent DMAs together.
Consume pending top- and bottom-half Samus tile definitions with DMA channel 1.
Each seven-byte definition supplies a 24-bit source followed by two byte counts;
the second part is optional and begins immediately after the first source range.
Top data targets VRAM $6000/$6100 and bottom data targets $6080/$6180.
Independently test the bottom-half request and repeat the same one- or two-part
descriptor transfer at the bottom-half VRAM destinations. A zero second size
skips only the optional second DMA.
When animated-tile objects are enabled, scan their six word-indexed slots from
$0A down to zero. A live object with a pending source address uploads its bank-$87
graphics through DMA channel 0 to the prepared VRAM word address.
Skip empty objects and slots with no newly prepared graphics. After a transfer,
clear only the source address so the request is consumed once while the animated
tile object itself remains active.
Any release or change in the complete input word reloads the initial repeat delay.
After that delay expires, the unchanged input word is copied to fake-new and the
shorter subsequent delay is reloaded. Real new-input remains edge-only.
The retained conditional debug path repeats the same edge/repeat bookkeeping for
controller 2, handles the four-button soft-reset chord when audio is not uploading,
and then interprets controller-1 debug chords without changing the ordinary sampler.
